chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Ibn Sinan, from Isma'il ibn 'Ammar, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
One obligatory salat (prayer) is better than twenty hajj pilgrimages, and one hajj pilgrimage is better than a house filled with gold from which charity is given until it is exhausted.

key_terms.بَيْتٍ: a house, used here as a measure of vast material wealth
key_terms.صَلَاةٌ: salat (prayer), the prescribed act of worship being praised here
key_terms.فَرِيضَةٌ: obligatory; indicating a divinely mandated duty
key_terms.يَفْنَى: it is exhausted or comes to an end

ai.seo_question: Why is one obligatory salat (prayer) considered better than many hajj pilgrimages and great charity?
ai.summary: This hadith emphasizes the immense merit of obligatory salat (prayer), placing it above repeated hajj in rank. It also shows the greatness of hajj, ranking it above giving away vast material wealth in charity, thereby highlighting the supreme value of divinely prescribed acts of worship.
